root_cause.text: The spi-sprd-adi probe path mixed unmanaged controller allocation via spi_alloc_host() with devm-managed registration via devm_spi_register_controller(), causing the error path to manually call spi_controller_put() on a controller that devres would also release on probe failure.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE/commit explicitly states that after devm_register_restart_handler() failure the code jumped to put_ctlr and called spi_controller_put(), while the controller had been registered with devm_spi_register_controller() so "the device core will automatically call spi_controller_put() again"; the patch fixes this by replacing spi_alloc_host() with devm_spi_alloc_host() and deleting the put_ctlr label and manual spi_controller_put() call.

agent_logs.evidence_points: The CVE/commit explicitly states that after devm_register_restart_handler() failure the code jumped to put_ctlr and called spi_controller_put(), while the controller had been registered with devm_spi_register_controller() so "the device core will automatically call spi_controller_put() again"; the patch fixes this by replacing spi_alloc_host() with devm_spi_alloc_host() and deleting the put_ctlr label and manual spi_controller_put() call.

intent_record.intent_summary: Use device-managed SPI host allocation in sprd_adi_probe to ensure automatic cleanup and avoid resource leaks.
intent_record.what: The probe function changes the SPI controller allocation call from spi_alloc_host(&pdev->dev, sizeof(struct sprd_adi)) to devm_spi_alloc_host(&pdev->dev, sizeof(struct sprd_adi)).
intent_record.how: This makes the allocated SPI host controller device-managed so it will be automatically freed when the device is detached or probe cleanup occurs, reducing the need for manual release and preventing resource leaks on error or removal paths.

intent_record.intent_summary: Simplify sprd_adi_probe() error handling by returning the ioremap failure directly instead of jumping to cleanup.
intent_record.what: The error handling after devm_platform_get_and_ioremap_resource() was simplified by replacing the block that assigned ret = PTR_ERR(sadi->base) and jumped to the put_ctlr label with a direct return PTR_ERR(sadi->base) when IS_ERR(sadi->base) is true.
intent_record.how: At runtime, a failed resource mapping now causes the probe function to return the error code immediately instead of branching to shared cleanup logic; this removes the put_ctlr path from this failure case and relies on the direct return behavior, likely because no additional cleanup is needed at that point.

intent_record.intent_summary: Simplify sprd_adi_probe() hwspinlock failure paths by returning directly instead of branching to shared cleanup.
intent_record.what: In sprd_adi_probe(), the error handling after devm_hwspin_lock_request_specific() and in the default branch of the hwlock-id switch was changed from assigning/logging and jumping to the put_ctlr label to returning directly: the '!sadi->hwlock' case now returns -ENXIO instead of setting ret and goto put_ctlr, and the default switch case now returns the result of dev_err_probe() instead of calling it and then goto put_ctlr.
intent_record.how: At runtime, probe now exits immediately on these hwspinlock-related failures instead of falling through shared cleanup via put_ctlr. This changes the error path behavior so these cases do not execute whatever additional cleanup or controller release logic exists at put_ctlr, relying instead on direct return and managed resource handling.

intent_record.intent_summary: Simplify probe error handling by returning dev_err_probe() directly and dropping redundant manual controller cleanup in the devm-managed path.
intent_record.what: The probe function replaces two error-handling blocks after devm_spi_register_controller() and devm_register_restart_handler() with direct returns using dev_err_probe(), and removes the shared put_ctlr label along with the explicit spi_controller_put(ctlr) and final return ret path.
intent_record.how: On failure to register the SPI controller or restart handler, the function now immediately returns the original error code while logging through dev_err_probe(); it no longer jumps to a cleanup label to call spi_controller_put(), relying on devm-managed resource handling instead.

grouping_result.intent: Use device-managed SPI host allocation in sprd_adi_probe to ensure automatic cleanup and avoid resource leaks.
Simplify probe error handling by returning dev_err_probe() directly and dropping redundant manual controller cleanup in the devm-managed path.

consistency_review.core_intent: Simplify sprd_adi_probe() probe error handling by returning failures directly, including dev_err_probe(), and removing unnecessary cleanup in devm-managed paths.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly addresses the root cause by replacing unmanaged spi_alloc_host() usage in the probe path with device-managed SPI host allocation, aligning allocation and registration lifetimes and preventing the double-release/error-path cleanup mismatch.

The changes directly remove redundant manual spi_controller cleanup in sprd_adi_probe() error paths while using devm-managed controller registration, matching the root cause of double-releasing the controller on probe failure.

candidates.rationale: This performs unmanaged SPI controller allocation, which is the root mismatch when later paired with devm-managed controller registration and cleanup.
This registers the controller with devres management, creating automatic cleanup on probe failure; combined with unmanaged allocation and manual put, it leads to double release.
This manual cleanup in the error path releases the controller even though devm_spi_register_controller() already arranges devres-based release on probe failure, directly causing the double put.
This branches probe failures into the shared manual cleanup path that calls spi_controller_put(), triggering the double-release after devm-managed registration has been set up.
These post-registration error paths route execution to the manual spi_controller_put() cleanup label, which is unsafe once the controller is already managed by devres.

vuln_statements.explanation: This manual error-path release is the direct vulnerable operation: after devm_spi_register_controller() has registered devres cleanup for the controller, probe failure will also trigger an automatic release, so this explicit put causes the double release described in the root cause.

This introduces devres-managed controller cleanup. In combination with unmanaged allocation and the later manual spi_controller_put(), it creates the conflicting ownership model that leads to double release on probe failure.

This allocates the SPI controller using unmanaged allocation. Mixing this with devm_spi_register_controller() later in the same probe path creates the ownership mismatch at the core of the vulnerability.

This routes post-registration probe errors into the shared cleanup label that manually calls spi_controller_put(), making the double release reachable once devm_spi_register_controller() has already installed devres cleanup.

diff --git a/drivers/spi/spi-sprd-adi.c b/drivers/spi/spi-sprd-adi.c
new file mode 100644
index 0000
bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable allocation/registration mismatch is visible directly in `sprd_adi_probe()`. The controller is allocated with unmanaged allocation: `ctlr = spi_alloc_master(&pdev->dev, sizeof(struct sprd_adi));`. Later it is registered with devres-managed registration: `ret = devm_spi_register_controller(&pdev->dev, ctlr);`. On failure paths after that registration attempt, the code goes to labels that manually release resources, including `put_ctlr:` followed by `spi_controller_put(ctlr);`. This is exactly the root cause described: mixing unmanaged `spi_alloc_*` with `devm_spi_register_controller()` so that probe failure can lead to a manual `spi_controller_put()` while devres also owns cleanup. There is no fix present such as switching to `__devm_spi_alloc_controller()` / `devm_spi_alloc_host()`-style allocation or using non-devm registration consistently.
